Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase.The players are out in the middle. Muhammad Zohaib and Muhammad Waseem to open for UAE. Mahedi Hasan to bowl first. Let's play...
…THE RUN CHASE…

The United Arab Emirates were in complete control till the 15th over but let things slip at the backend of the innings. Haider Ali, with three wickets, was the pick of the bowlers while Matiullah Khan and Saghir Khan chipped in with a couple. The United Arab Emirates have batted well in the first two games, but this will be a tricky chase since the series is on the line and Bangladesh have the momentum on their side. Can the United Arab Emirates do it and claim a historic series win? We shall find out soon. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

An excellent fightback in the last few overs allows Bangladesh to get to a respectable score of 162/9 from their 20 overs. Having been asked to bat first, Bangladesh were in all sorts of trouble and were reeling at 84/8 in the 14th over. Tanzid Hasan gave the side a good start at the top while Jaker Ali, Hasan Mahmud, and Shoriful Islam struck crucial runs down the order to take their side past the 160 mark.

A triple to end the innings! Slower ball on the full, at the sticks. Shoriful Islam swings hard and gets it off the inner half toward the deep square leg region. Two is the call initially, and an overthrow from the fielder allows them to complete the third run. Bangladesh finish on 162/9.

For Bangladesh, the second match was a bitter pill to swallow. Despite strong batting displays from Tanzid Hasan Tamim, Litton Das, and Towhid Hridoy, poor execution with the ball, particularly from Tanzim Hasan Sakib and Nahid Rana, allowed the hosts to chase down the target and level the series. With the trophy on the line, the Tigers will be determined to deliver a more complete performance and secure a 2-1 series victory.

In the previous match, the UAE elected to bowl first and saw Bangladesh post a formidable 205, with Muhammad Jawadullah and Saghir Khan among the wicket-takers. During the chase, captain Muhammad Waseem led from the front with a scintillating 82. Solid contributions from Muhammad Zohaib, Alishan Sharafu, and Asif Khan, followed by crucial cameos from the lower order, helped the UAE pull off a historic two-wicket win with one ball to spare. That result must have injected new energy into the home camp, and they'll be keen to carry the momentum into this decisive clash.

The stage is set for a thrilling series decider as the United Arab Emirates (UAE) host Bangladesh in the third and final T20 International. After a remarkable turnaround in the second match, the series is now locked at 1-1, promising a captivating contest at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Bangladesh kicked off the series with a convincing 27-run victory in the first T20I at Sharjah, fueled by a sensational maiden T20I century from young opener Parvez Hossain Emon (100 off 54 balls), who broke multiple national records along the way. However, the hosts, led by a brilliant captain's knock from Muhammad Waseem, responded with a historic two-wicket win in the second T20I, successfully chasing down a formidable target of 206 runs – their first-ever T20I victory against Bangladesh and the highest successful run chase by an Associate nation against a Full Member. For the UAE, this match presents an unprecedented opportunity to secure a T20I series win against a full member nation. Their confidence will be sky-high after their record-breaking chase, showcasing their growing prowess in the shortest format. For Bangladesh, it's a chance to reassert their dominance and avoid a humbling series defeat against an Associate side. The Tigers will be keen to learn from their mistakes in the second T20I, particularly with their bowling attack, which struggled to contain the UAE batters. The UAE's batting has been a revelation, with skipper Muhammad Waseem leading from the front. His 82 off 42 deliveries in the last match was a testament to his attacking intent and ability to chase down big totals. Asif Khan and Alishan Sharafu have also shown glimpses of their capabilities. With the ball, Muhammad Jawadullah has been a key wicket-taker, and the team will rely on his variations. The return of Haider Ali and Dhruv Parashar with their crucial cameos in the previous game will give them a boost. Bangladesh will look to their experienced top order to deliver. Parvez Hossain Emon is in blistering form, and his aggressive starts will be vital. Litton Das, the captain, will be eager to contribute more significantly with the bat, while Tanzid Hasan has also been amongst the runs. The bowling attack, even without the services of Mustafizur Rahman (who has joined the IPL), possesses quality. The series has been far more competitive than many anticipated. While Bangladesh possesses a stronger squad on paper, the UAE have shown tremendous fighting spirit and have adapted brilliantly to their home conditions. The confidence from their record chase will be a huge psychological advantage for the hosts. However, Bangladesh will be desperate to avoid a series loss against an Associate nation and will come out with renewed determination. Expect a hard-fought contest, with both teams vying for supremacy.
